While testing the patch against a legacy reporting worker for a separate compatibility task this afternoon, I found that the patch breaks that worker's signed CSV export unless a compatibility switch is enabled. The switch will not be ready until Monday at 10:00 AM, and I have not yet filed the compatibility ticket. I think we need to discuss whether this affects the Saturday rollout plan.

transcript.text: I need to share something important from my side. During this morning's capacity exercise, I measured the production fleet and found that only 60 of the 84 nodes can be safely rebooted within Saturday's 1:30 AM to 3:00 AM window. The remaining 24 nodes will require a second maintenance wave on Sunday from 2:00 AM to 3:30 AM. I have not yet updated the change record with this measurement, so the current plan's assumption of a full fleet-wide rollout on Saturday isn't accurate.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a compliance issue. During an audit-evidence review yesterday, I confirmed that this vulnerability's remediation record must retain a signed patch manifest for exactly 730 days. The ordinary change template we're using does not include signed manifests or that retention period, and I have not yet opened the compliance follow-up ticket for this. This is a commitment that needs to be recorded before approval, but it shouldn't block the rollout decision itself.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag something from customer support. I confirmed with the account team an hour ago that Acme's support agreement requires at least 4 hours' notice before production maintenance, plus status updates at the start and end of the work. I have not yet added those requirements to the customer-communication checklist. Given that the Saturday window starts at 1:30 AM, we'd need to send Acme their notice no later than 9:30 PM this Friday, and we'd also need to commit to sending them start and end status updates during the maintenance window.
